text:
lydia: Punting from the RFC meeting  - we need a concrete rollout metadata schema that supports: stable routing, controlled aliasing, and a safe rollback anchor. Drafting this thread to capture ideas.

marco: Agree. High level constraints: immutable content identity (content_hash), opaque stable_id for routing, and human-friendly aliases. We also need a minimal remap surface for ops.

reza: One concrete idea: require each catalog entry to publish 3 canonical fields: `stable_id` (opaque), `content_hash` (sha256:...), and `alias_list` (flattened list of alias=name|stable_id pairs). Clients may pin by stable_id or alias.

nia: Ops note: alias remaps must be auditable and rate-limited. If we let aliases point to stable_ids directly we should also publish `remap_token` and `remap_timestep`. That way control-plane can verify if the client cache is stale.

lydia: I sketched a minimal example for the RFC follow-up: ```json
{
  "stable_id": "sid-0a1b-2c3d",
  "content_hash": "sha256:012345abcdef...",
  "alias_list": ["latest=sid-0a1b-2c3d", "canary=sid-9f8e-7d6c"],
  "fallback_order": ["stable_id","content_hash","compatible_variant","rollback_anchor"],
  "rollback_anchor": "sid-0f0f-0f0f",
  "remap_token": "rt-20260320-7",
  "remap_timestep": "2026-03-20T15:04:05Z",
  "deprecation_notice": "remove-by:2026-09-01; message: 'migrate to gpt-lite-v3'"
}
```

marco: fallback_order is great. Runtime should never infer order implicitly. Also, require that `rollback_anchor` be an explicit stable_id that has passed safety tests. No wildcards.

reza: small API design question: should control-plane accept alias pins but resolve server-side and return effective_stable_id in response headers? That avoids client confusion.

nia: yes, server-side resolution + `X-Effective-Stable-Id` header and `X-Remap-Token` would be ideal. Clients cache both with a TTL. If remap_token changes, clients must re-resolve.

lydia: TTL discussion: two useful modes - session and fixed_seconds. Session = per process lifecycle; fixed_seconds = explicit TTL value. Proposal: default to session for SDKs, fixed_seconds for lightweight tools. Include `resolution_ttl_seconds` in metadata.

marco: Ops caution: long TTLs make emergency remaps slow to propagate. Recommend default 300s (5m) unless flagged `infrastructure_critical=true`.

reza: also define explicit error codes for mismatch scenarios: 409 for content-hash mismatch, 410 for deprecation, 424 for remap-in-progress. Helps clients implement deterministic retry behavior.

nia: governance: alias updates require two ACL checks: (1) write permission for alias namespace, (2) signed-off-by must include rollout lead when remapping alias pointing to a stable_id with failing `stability_score` < 80. We'll record the sign-off in `remap_token` metadata.

lydia: I want to add `stability_score` field and `compatibility` enum: {"compatible", "maybe-breaking", "breaking"}. Runtime uses these only for metrics and gating; policy layer enforces push rules.

marco: Implementation note: avoid nested objects in the transport payload for some lightweight clients. Use flattened key formats like `alias.latest=sid-...` and `alias.canary=sid-...` or an encoded list as lydia showed. But RFC should include both canonical JSON model and a transport encoding appendix.

reza: Migration for existing semver pins: catalog should start including stable_id in the listing; control-plane should auto-resolve legacy name pins and respond with `X-Effective-Stable-Id`. Publish a 90-day deprecation window where name pinning is accepted but clients receive more prominent deprecation warnings.

nia: Don't forget logging/auditing: every served request must log requested_pin, effective_stable_id, remap_token, and reason if fallback used. This is critical for postmortems.

lydia: Action items: (lydia) open RFC follow-up PR with schema + transport appendix; (marco) design header contract for `X-Effective-Stable-Id` and error codes; (reza) prototype runtime fallback respecting `fallback_order`; (nia) draft remap ACLs and rate-limit policy.

infra-bot: note: catalog-service v3.3 feature flag `alias-remap-audit` enabled on staging.

marco: One more subtlety: when alias resolves to a stable_id, we should also return `effective_content_hash` so clients can verify artifacts they have pre-warmed locally. This helps on-prem/private deployments.

reza: Agreed. I'll add `effective_content_hash` to the resolution response and runtime will validate before applying a large cache of weight artifacts.

lydia: Great thread. I'll include a short pseudocode snippet in the RFC for client resolution behavior and failure handling. Example: ```
// client initialization
if ("pin looks like stable_id") use it
else {
  resp = resolveAlias(pin) // returns effective_stable_id, remap_token, ttl
  cache(resp.effective_stable_id, resp.remap_token, ttl)
}
// on 409/content-mismatch -> re-resolve immediately, unless remap_token unchanged -> fail hard
```

nia: closing notes: ensure we have a dashboard for alias_mismatch_count and remap_latency. ops will need an alert if remap_latency spikes beyond threshold.

lydia: OK closing. i'll open the PR and ping you all. Thanks! :thumbsup:
